s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of sharp precordial pain with persistent symptoms and abnormal cardiac sounds
salient_findings: Sporadic clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge
key_facts: 19-year-old man with no past medical history
Three-week history of persistent sharp precordial pain
Pain began during an episode of gastroenteritis
Gastrointestinal symptoms resolved while chest pain remained
Pain is mild and worsens on inspiration
Sporadic clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge
Normal vital signs
Normal lung and heart auscultation except for intermittent clicking
Normal laboratory studies, including arterial blood gas analysis, complete blood count, C-reactive protein, D-dimer level, and cardiac troponins
Normal chest radiograph
Electrocardiography showed a sinus rhythm at 78 bpm with a normal QRS duration and axis

shortlist.label: Mitral valve prolapse
shortlist.why_kept: Intermittent clicking sound over the left sternal border

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Sharp precordial pain that worsens on inspiration

shortlist.label: Costochondritis
shortlist.why_kept: Precordial pain and clicking sound, normal cardiac examination

shortlist.label: Precordial catch syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Sharp precordial pain and normal cardiac examination

shortlist.label: Tietze syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Precordial pain and clicking sound, normal laboratory studies

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of sharp precordial pain that worsens on inspiration, along with a sporadic clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge, are consistent with Precordial catch syndrome. The normal laboratory studies and electrocardiography also support this diagnosis, as Precordial catch syndrome is a benign condition that does not typically have abnormal lab results or ECG findings.

rejected.label: Mitral valve prolapse
rejected.why: Typically associated with a mid-systolic click and murmur on auscultation, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: Usually presents with diffuse chest pain that improves with sitting up and leaning forward, and is often accompanied by a pericardial friction rub, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Costochondritis
rejected.why: Typically presents with tenderness to palpation of the costochondral junctions, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Tietze syndrome
rejected.why: Similar to costochondritis, but typically presents with swelling and tenderness of the costochondral junctions, which is not present in this case
